03

Cryptocurrency, Token and Web3 Risks

Digital assets and decentralised technologies are experimental, volatile and may be difficult to understand. Their risks can include, without limitation:

  • Price volatility: token and cryptocurrency prices can rise or fall rapidly, including to zero.
  • Loss of funds: transactions may be irreversible, incorrectly addressed, delayed, blocked or permanently lost.
  • Liquidity risk: a token may have little or no market, buyers, sellers or ability to convert it into cash.
  • Technology risk: smart-contract bugs, exploits, bridge failures, consensus failures, network outages or software defects may cause loss or interruption.
  • Project risk: a team may stop development, change its model, abandon a network, fail to deliver, or become unavailable.
  • Regulatory and tax risk: rules, tax treatment and the legal status of digital assets can differ by location and may change.
  • Fraud risk: phishing, impersonation, rug pulls, fake tokens, malicious applications and misleading promotions may target participants.

Past performance, past rewards, historic token prices, previous payouts, community popularity or a project's continued operation do not guarantee future performance or results. You can lose all funds, tokens, fees, hardware costs, electricity costs, time and other resources committed to an activity.

04

DePIN Projects, Nodes, Hardware and Bandwidth

Total Crypto Hub may describe decentralised compute, storage, bandwidth, wireless, mapping, sensor, edge-device and other physical-infrastructure networks. Participation in these networks may require you to install software, run a node, provide computing resources, connect devices, share bandwidth, maintain uptime or purchase hardware.

These activities can involve costs and risks, including:

  • Hardware purchase, maintenance, repair, replacement, depreciation and compatibility issues.
  • Electricity, cooling, internet, data usage, hosting, transaction, withdrawal and other operating fees.
  • Uncertain node uptime requirements, changing reward formulas, reduced incentives, network congestion or device restrictions.
  • ISP contract restrictions, local network rules, bandwidth caps, service interruptions and possible impacts on your connection.
  • Device security, malware, unauthorised access, data exposure, privacy concerns and misuse of an internet connection.
  • Geographic restrictions, identity checks, minimum thresholds, lockups, payout delays or changes to project eligibility.

We do not control the operation, reward policy, technical design, security, eligibility rules or continued existence of third-party DePIN networks. A node guide, setup tutorial, project listing or hardware description is informational only. Check the project's official documentation and your device, ISP, local rules and personal circumstances before proceeding.

There is no guarantee that running a node, providing bandwidth, storage, compute power or other resources will generate rewards or recover your costs. You may spend money and resources and receive nothing in return.

05

Airdrops, Testnets, Quests and Campaigns

Information about airdrops, testnets, quests, points programmes, referral campaigns, giveaways, early access opportunities and community tasks may be displayed for discovery and educational purposes. Total Crypto Hub does not control the campaign organisers and does not guarantee that a campaign is genuine, active, available in your region or worthwhile.

Participation may require time, wallet connections, transactions, personal information, identity verification, referrals, social-media activity or payment of network fees. Rewards may be changed, delayed, reduced, cancelled, restricted or never distributed. Points, testnet tokens and campaign badges may have no monetary value and may never become transferable or redeemable.

Always check the official campaign rules, eligibility criteria, deadlines, geographic restrictions and announcement channels. Be cautious of fake claim pages, impersonators, urgent messages and requests for seed phrases or private keys. Never pay an unverified person to “unlock” an airdrop or guaranteed reward.

Wallets, Exchanges, Token Information and Smart Token Tools

The Website may list or discuss wallets, exchanges, token tools, token checkers, blockchain explorers and related services. These references are provided to help visitors find information. They do not mean that Total Crypto Hub owns, operates, controls, audits or endorses those services.

Wallets and exchanges may be custodial or non-custodial and may involve different risks. You are responsible for checking the provider, downloading software only from authentic sources, protecting your account and understanding the permissions and transactions you approve. An exchange may suspend withdrawals, restrict accounts, become insolvent or suffer a security incident. A wallet may be compromised or become inaccessible.

Token names, tickers, contract addresses, network details, liquidity information, holder data, verification indicators and other token-related information can be incomplete, delayed, inaccurate or confused by counterfeit tokens with similar names. Always independently verify the exact blockchain network and contract address through reliable official sources before interacting with a token or smart contract.

A result shown by a token finder, token checker or other Website tool is not a security audit, investment recommendation, guarantee of legitimacy or confirmation that a token is safe to buy, hold or use. Automated checks and publicly available data can miss malicious behaviour and emerging risks.

Actual results can be very different because of token prices, network difficulty, reward rates, uptime, hardware performance, fees, electricity and internet costs, withdrawal limits, taxes, exchange rates, location, eligibility and changes made by a project. 12

Security, Wallet Safety and Anti-Scam Warning

Crypto and Web3 users are frequent targets for phishing, fake support accounts, impersonation, malicious browser extensions, fake applications, fraudulent token claims and social-engineering attacks. Scammers may copy our name, logo, content or the names of projects listed on the Website.

  • Never share your wallet seed phrase, recovery phrase, private keys, passwords or one-time authentication codes with anyone.
  • Never send funds to a person claiming they must receive payment to verify, unlock, recover or guarantee your rewards.
  • Check website addresses, social handles, contract addresses and downloadable files carefully; use official sources that you have independently confirmed.
  • Be suspicious of urgent messages, guaranteed profits, unusually high returns, unsolicited direct messages and fake customer-support accounts.
  • Review wallet permissions and transaction details before signing. A transaction may grant access to tokens or assets and may be irreversible.

Total Crypto Hub and Total Crypto Network will never ask you to provide your wallet seed phrase, private keys or passwords through the Website, email or direct messages. If you encounter a suspicious account or message claiming to represent us, do not respond or transfer funds. Verify communication through contact details published on the official Website.
